tips.comment: Naval Light was hampered by a slow start and could never get close to Charles Darwin at Royal Ascot over 5f but could improve for going up in distance to 6f.

Race 6 at Goodwood is the British Stallion Stakes - Maiden for 2-year-olds over 1,207 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 2yo colt Bayraq Almuhamadia from the Richard Hannon yard and will be ridden by Sean Levey. This son of Sergei Prokofiev is making his debut here, and there is every reason to believe that he has some class coming from the Richard Hannon yard. Worthy of inclusion in this field.

Made an encouraging debut at Newbury in a 6.5f minor event, finishing 4th without coming under too much pressure when making late headway. Still looked in need of the experience at Haydock last time when 7th stepping up to 7f. Capable of better and should feature more prominently this time despite dropping back to 6f.
Improved on a poor debut performance to finish a good 4th at Ffos Las 3 weeks ago. Further improvement is likely, and that gives an each-way chance.

I've been all over this one twice already as has three siblings out of dam that all won on their second starts and looked an early sort on paper. Was punted heavily last time but never threatened but is interesting Kieren Shoemark keeps the faith. Has shown ability in both starts and I would be kicking myself for not backing this one or putting him up after fancying him strongly the last twice. Might of needed the runs anyway and interesting owner runs here as well as shorter priced runner but can go well before tackling handicaps. Yard had a 2yo winner recently and small ew play for me in one that has been on my radar.
Quite simply Illinois should be odds-on. He's been runner-up in three Group 1's & this drop back to 2m from the 2m4f of the Ascot Gold Cup trip should clinch his first win at the top level.

Scandinavia is not the choice of Ryan Moore for this Group 1 as Ascot Gold Cup 2nd Illinois is chosen from Aidan O'Brien's pair in this race. Nevertheless, Scandinavia looks progressive and put up a very fast time when winning the Group 3 Bahrain Trophy over 13f at Newmarket last time, winning by nearly nine lengths, and could give Illinois a race.

Won a very competitive handicap here in May and needed all of the 1m6f trip there to get up so step up to 2m here looks sure to suit. Stepped up another notch when winning the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot and again showed stamina might be his forte. Another step forward is needed here but is going the right way and has a good strike rate of four wins from 6 races. Interesting yard run him here as well as last year's second Sweet William when he could of stayed at a lower level so could be the one to serve it up to O'Brien's duo. Course winner warrants a close eye and could be the fly in the ointment.

Which one of the Gosden trio will come out on top? All have a chance, and I think they are good enough to see off the challenge from Ireland. This one is a consistent type and looks good each way value.

The Gosden team have 3 runners in this and Military Academy looks the outisder of all. He is yet to race beyond a mile and a half but the yard must be confident he will get the trip to race him. William Buick takes the ride and he could go well at a decent price.

Sunway is closely matched with Illinois at his best, finishing not far behind him in the Leger. He looks a bit below the very best at a mile and a half, so this looks worth a shout for him to try and match Illinois’ already impressive first effort over significantly further. Goodwood is a good place to try it, I think, as Sunway, I've thought, has always looked a fairly nimble horse that could appreciate a slog of a run in at this tricky track. He slugged it out well last time, but the way he finished in the Leger just suggests he might come into his own over this new trip. Scandinavia is surely to be feared getting a stone.
Dubai Future was third when 7L behind Illinois last time out in a G1 at 2m4f on GF. I am relying on the drop back to 2 miles on Good to get a bit closer EW.

Dorset is a 2-year-old colt trained by A P O'Brien. He has a nice profile, putting up a promising debut run at the Curragh, beaten 1/2 length by stablemate Amadeus Mozart despite being slowly away, only to get the hang of things late on. He is out of a dam sired by Galileo called Snowflakes, who was a half-sister to the A P O'Brien trained Winter, who won four Group 1's, which included the English and Irish 1000 Guineas, the Coronation Stakes, and the Nassau Stakes at Goodwood. Dorset won impressively on his next start at the Curragh, beating stablemate Benvenuto Cellini (2.75 lengths ahead of the rest), a colt who was unchallenged next time out and holds multiple pattern race entries. Dorset is my short-priced banker of the day under Ryan Moore.
If you are able to move past the hotpot for the Aiden O'Brien yard, Humidity really looks to be the horse to side with in this race. Good value too.

If ever there was a horse suited by Jamie Spencer, then this could well be it, judged by his easy win last time out when held up and finishing with a real rattle. That wasn't just any race either; it was a hot class 2 at Ascot. A look through the previous winners of that race and their respective winning times reveals that this horse clocked a really quick time and has plenty of gears. So there's no way he should be a double-figure price here, in my opinion, especially since that was his debut and he'll no doubt have come on for the run.

Do Or Do Not is still a maiden, but he has run on well to finish 2nd in his last three races over 6f. The move up to 7f should suit him. His last two races were 2nd to Gstaad in the Group 2 Coventry at Royal Ascot, followed by 2nd to Zavateri in the Group 2 July Stakes at Newmarket. He could reverse that on three-pound better terms.

A Palace Pier colt. He is a half-brother to the successful winner Magnum Opus, who has won up to 9f. The dam is a winner at distances between 11.5f and 15f. He showed promise despite being inexperienced, finishing 7th in a competitive Newbury maiden race, and then improved for 7f when he secured a victory in a Haydock novice race 2 weeks later. There is potential for improvement, which looks encouraging with the Gosden stable in great form and the selection of William Buick to ride. Considering Buick's current form and his 21% win rate at Goodwood, the 20/1 odds for this distance winner appear to be quite favorable. However, it looks like a wise choice for an each-way bet.

Some obvious cases in here, but one less so I thought was Gharma Sutra, who goes 2nd time up for Hannon. Now, he’s beaten a horse 7-8L that Do Or Do Not has beaten slightly further, having had a run under him. So whilst any of these could improve, there was something not quite right about having this horse as the rank outsider as a result. The debut win was all the more impressive given he’s done it from a wide draw, been keen early, and not seen a rival from pillar to post. It’s unlikely he will get any sort of easy lead here, but with an interesting mix of speed and stamina, he looks a versatile sort that is capable of springing a surprise at a price. If he improves for the run just two weeks ago, much like a few of these, he could well prove to be anything, especially if he can settle a bit better over this longer trip.

Kinross has a great record in this race (2 wins) and showed that this 8-year-old still is a force to be reckoned with when finishing second last time on seasonal debut at Haydock in a Group 3 carrying a penalty. No penalty this time and must go close.

Audience hacked up by an eased down four lengths in this race last year when carrying a five-pound penalty for having also won the Group 1 Lockinge earlier in the season. He has not been in the same form yet this season but cannot be overlooked, drawn well in stall 4 with both Jonquil and Kinross drawn wide.
Back over the longer trip, Jonquil should be able to put a line through the last race and improve to win this race here.

Race 3 at Goodwood today is the World Pool Lennox Stakes - Group 2 for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,408 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old colt Noble Champion from the Ed Walker yard, and will be ridden by Kieran Shoemark. This son of Lope De Vega has a touch of class about him and showed some real mettle in his latest when cruising home to win the Gr3 Jersey Stakes at Ascot last month by 3 lengths. He should have a say in this field and should be included in everything.

Lake Forest is a 4-year-old colt trained by William Haggas. He has 3 wins out of 11 and thrives on good to firm ground. He is a winner of a Group 2 at York in 2023 and won the Golden Eagle Stakes in Australia in November 2024 on good ground over 7.5f, beating a horse called Lazzat, who has 8 wins out of 11. Lazzat, since that defeat at Rosehill (Aus), won a Listed race in France by 5.5 lengths, posting an RPR of 125, and then came to UK shores and won the Group 1 Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at Ascot, posting a RPR of 124. Lake Forest finished a creditable Group 1 fifth at Royal Ascot (114), and the subsequent run at York may have come too soon. He has the form to figure today, particularly if we have a blistering pace, as he stays 7f better than most of his rivals.

Beat Kinross on return run when taking a Grp3 @ Haydock and had useful form @ Grp2 level last season. Should come on for that run, world class jockey retains ride and in hands of a very good trainer, making current 10/1 solid Ew value in the race.
Quinault has only had four runs this year but did get into the groove with a G3 win last time out. I think this puts him in with an EW 4P shout at a G2.

Backing Witness Stand, the 4-year-old Expert Eye colt trained by Dr. Richard Newland & Jamie Insole, in tomorrow’s highly competitive Group 2 feature. Despite encountering stronger company lately, his profile and course experience make him a well-shaped each-way candidate. His latest outing was a narrow second at Chester over 7f, where he led until 2f out and was headed only close to the line??'strong put-in against a good level of opposition (~11/1 at the time). Historically, he’s carried front-running tactics well: a Listed winner at Newbury last season and solid form figures of 16-062, largely featuring course and distance experience at Goodwood and Chester. Rated 110, he enters this top-class event with a mark that reflects upside. Though up against rivals with more Group race experience, such as Kinross and Jonquil, Witness Stand thrives when allowed to dictate terms and potentially unsettle the pace-makers.
Showed his level of ability when bagging an impressive win at Haydock back in May of this year and given his ability, does look to be a bit overpriced for me, despite going up in class.

A fairly open event, 3/1 the field, and plenty of lines into it with enough doubts about many to take on the top of the market. Perhaps a less well-trodden one is Iberian, who has posted a peak career speed figure at Ascot last time coming from last to fifth. He faded late, suggesting a step up a furlong isn’t an obvious move, but this is a different track to Ascot clearly. He’s placed 2nd here behind Haatem as a 2yo, so there should be no fear he won’t appreciate it either. He’s got bundles to find on ratings, but I just think he’s been shaping better in his races than his finishing positions suggest, and his penultimate run can be ignored as he missed the kick completely. His run prior to that was excellent and he would have won had he not drifted left and got spooked by Spycatcher, and whilst that’s not the level of form to win this, there’s still scope for improvement in him enough to take a small chance.

Joined David O'Meara following Michael Stoute's retirement and has good form in the book. Three length Listed winner over 1 mile at Newmarket on first start at age three before running second in a Group 3 here. Second in a Group 3 over 7f at Newmarket again last year. Disappointing in two starts for new yard so far. Dropped back to seven furlongs and return to Goodwood can perhaps help turn things around. Jason Watson rides.

Beat 23 rivals in a handicap at Ascot and ran well in a group 3 at Sandown. Stable is in flying form and Oisin Murphy knows the horse well and is himself back in good form after a bit of a wobble. Great each way chance with 6 places back in a handicap.

Redorange won a C3 in May, and in the two runs since, has been close but no cigar. So, he is climbing up the weights without winning, but the latest run was only ¾L away from the winner when fourth. I think the expected rain today will help his cause while just 1 lb heavier.
Jamie Spencer is retained on Jakajaro and he looked unlucky last time at Ascot when his path through to the leaders became blocked in the last furlong and he could only finish 6th of 17.

Won over today's C/D @ this meeting last year and has put up 4 very good efforts this season without winning, including @ Grp3 level Lto. Looks primed to run well in this class 2 handicap, top jockey back up who does not normally ride for this stable and in hands of a very shrewd trainer, making current 7.50 very good Ew value here.

Canon's House is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Michael and David Easterby and ridden by Christoph Soumillon. He turned over a new leaf in 2023, winning three consecutive sprints and rising from a handicap mark of 63 to 89. He finished 10th out of 18 in a valuable 6.5f 50k handicap at the Curragh and was sent off as short as 11-2 behind some smart Irish sprinters. He took a keen hold in that race and soon led, pressing the leader after 2f but weakened inside the final furlong. Dropping back down to 5f today off a 2lb lower handicap mark, Canon's House should be seen to better effect. He beat Woohoo (received 27lb from Canon's House) on a previous start at Hamilton by a comfortable 1.5 lengths, a sprinter who had won his previous three starts and has since won again. He is likely to be let loose from the front given his racing style and can confirm that he's still a progressive sprinter in the making.

Loves this track, winner of three of her five starts here, second and fifth in the other two. This is a much tougher assignment, but the showers forecast for the morning are in her favor, and that course form is a big plus.

On a workable mark and has run well on more than one occasion here in the past. Beat American Affair at Ponte last summer from this mark, with that horse now a stone higher in weights and winning at Royal Ascot. Looks to be good each-way value here.

Kevin Ryan likes to lay one out for a big handicap and hopefully this is another. This race isn't littered with well handicapped types and I think this outsider could surprise since last Summer he was racing off marks at around 91/92 before having a wind op. He races now off 87 with a new jockey booked who I actually prefer to many of the jockeys the stable usually uses. A fast ground 5 furlongs is ideal, and he could well be in the mix so the 20/1 will do for an e/w bet.

Brazen Bolt has 9 wins from 41 starts and looks interesting at these odds. He has been in excellent form this year, being placed twice at Doncaster in June and then winning a 16 handicap at York last month. That was a Class 4, and he is up to Class 2 level off 3lbs higher at 83. He has, however, won off 87, and with Warren Fentiman claiming 5lbs, he looks like a good EW bet with 6 places on offer.

One pound lower than for win here in May this year and excuses for all three starts since (lost shoes, blindfold off late last time). This 4yo Harry Angel gelding requires a skilled jockey in the saddle and a bit of luck. Might really appreciate low draw in stall 1 (veered right for his win here earlier this year).
Wheels of Fire has been a big disappointment after looking like he was really offering something to work with. The yard is persisting with these better races and he has to have a good chance here.

This could be a straight shootout between Adrestia and Redorange as the market suggests, but a wild sprint can’t go without backing one at a bigger price. Paddy’s Day was in behind a few of these at Ascot, but raced on the wrong side of the track, ultimately with the stands side having all the front-ranked horses home best. That was run in a quick time, on ground that wouldn’t have been ideal for this horse. He’s much better with at least some juice in it, as proven by his recent effort on good ground when not far behind the reopposing Mon Na Slieve at Musselburgh. He confirmed his well-being with a peak AW RPR on his penultimate start, so if he takes to the track on more suitable ground, I think he can outrun these odds despite there being chances all over. I don’t mind a draw on the low side, and he’s got enough pace around him to give him something to aim at.

Twilight Jet did not win last year and was mainly running in Group/Listed company but changed yards and returned from a break in May with a switch to C2 handicaps with improvement when second up and could be worth another shot EW 6P.

A Swedish horse, making his UK debut. He has finished in the first two 10 times from 12 starts on turf, winning 9 times from 6 to 7 furlongs, and he drops to 5 furlongs today, on good going which should suit. Carlos Lopez is his regular jockey who is booked to ride.

The key to these races is often to check on the quality of horses that the selection has beat and the quality of those that have finished close to them. This filly for example, was always in command when winning her maiden at Newmarket and the 3rd and 4th have shown enough since to give that race a stamp of quality. The 4th for example was sent off 2nd fav for a Listed race when rated 102 and this all stacks up well for Zgharta to go close here off just 89.
Ran an impressive 5th in the Sandringham LTO, and that's good prep for this race. Plenty of winners usually come out of that, and the trainer does well at this festival.

Ran well here in an apprentice race at the beginning of June before going on to win at Kempton, then again at York. The York win was impressive and looked to have plenty more in the tank when winning unchallenged. Further improvement looked on the cards for the trainer who won this race in 2018 and 2020.

The 3yo filly has 1 win from 4. She was a close 4th of 10 in a Listed contest last time out, tired in the last 100 yards and this shorter trip can suit her. The 3rd has since won a Listed contest and the winner has since won a Group 2. The selection now drops into a handicap contest, her mark of 92 is very attractive and more improvement is very possible after just four career runs and a recent 10 week break.

Has been running very well this season and that includes Lto, when they were very unlucky in running, coming 2/6 beaten a neck in a class 4 handicap over extended mile @ Beverley. Only beaten 3 lengths in a class 2 @ Ascot 4 runs back, under used jockey who won on selection 3 runs ago is back up and in hands of a very good trainer, making current 11/1 the Ew value in the race.

Saffie Osborne takes the ride for Charlie Johnston on Blessed Star, who is still a maiden. She has finished 2nd four times and 3rd once in her five races to date. Her handicap mark of 77 looks workable for her to be competitive here.
Tundra Rose had shown significant ability at first but then just seemed to fail to capitalize on that on turf. But I don't think you can give up on this horse just yet with 4 places available.

Bountiful has had two midfield runs in C2 since the break, with the latest being to fourth. Although 1 lb lighter for this, she drops to C3, which does put her at top weight. But I think she could still be worth an EW with 4P on offer.

Unexposed 4yo filly, five career runs, form 23/1-14. She was an unlucky 4th of 15 three weeks ago in a similar class 3 handicap, losing places in the last 100 yards, over 7f. The drop back to 6f should suit her. However, she did race very wide with no cover for the first two furlongs that day and pulled too hard, but entering the final 2f she was still travelling far better than all her 14 rivals. Same mark for this handicap and Oisin Murphy now takes over in the saddle.

Woodhay Wonder has not won since May 2024 when she recorded her fourth win in a row at Newmarket. However, she has gradually been falling back towards her last winning mark of 93 and is now just a pound above it. She may be capable of going close at Goodwood.

The very capable Quinn stable always targets this meeting with some of their better horses, particularly their sprinters. That looks like the case again with Easy Peeler. She didn't get the best passage at Chester last time, so that run can be set aside. Prior to that, she went off favorite at Thirsk. However, there was quite a bit of rain before the race was run, and her chance was negated. She won a decent fillies' handicap at York before that, and I could see a similar outcome here.
Won over course and distance last year as a two year old. She beat the re-opposing Lady Of Andros over this trip at Chester last time out and likely further improvement to come from this filly.

Looked seriously in need of the run on his return at Haydock when finishing last of the 7 runners over 5f. Had shown better form over 6f on his final start on the AW last year and duly did so again next time at York when a close-up 5th, beaten less than 2 lengths before going down in a photo finish at Chester last time. This slightly more conventional track is a plus and is well worth considering.

Maybe better known as a Aw performer, but good efforts back on turf last 2 runs and that includes a very good run in this class 3 grade here @ Goodwood over 5f. They have plenty of early pace and are a distance winner so this easy 6f is not an issue, good apprentice who has ridden some nice touches for this stable is back up and trained by one of the shrewdest in the business, making current 12/1 decent Ew value here.

Has made the frame in each of her three starts since joining this yard and has been beaten in photo finishes the last three times. Her mark remains the same here and she is interesting in first time cheekpieces.

Karl Burke's horses are just beginning to run into form, and I think his Greydreambeliever has an each-way chance here in this Fillies Handicap. Last time out, she made up a lot of ground when staying on close home, finishing fourth in a similar race to this at Newmarket.

The William Haggas stable has been on fire recently. In the last couple of weeks, he has had a 35% strike rate, and he can have another winner here with Castle Cove, who was a comfortable winner from one of today's rivals when making his seasonal debut at Chester last month.

Was a huge eyecatcher for me last time at Epsom and went straight into my notebook as really ran a race full of promise after a year off. Stayed on really well and I actually backed him for the John Smiths Cup at York where if he had won would of landed me a right old punt as had a tidy double with Prince of India earlier in the week. Sadly didn't go there so have to steam in again given my earlier thoughts. Has handled Epsom so should handle here and draw ok too as last year's first four home were drawn 17, 13, 12, and 11. Big chance if coming on for the run.
Has got a substantial amount of upside remaining and, on balance, should be the one to side with in this pretty open field. Great chance.

Was a dual handicap winner for J. Murtagh in Ireland and this Irish raider has won their last 2 decent handicaps in good fashion for current stable , so should be up to this good class 2 event. Very good upcoming jockey is back up and top trainer who is in great form @ present, does not send them over unless he thinks they have a big chance, making current 8/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Winner of his last race and should follow up. Jockey in form, distance no problem. Second to Castle Cove but should turn the tables this time around. A great each way bet at 12/1, Nap Each Way.

Tony Montana is versatile over a mile and remains consistent at this level, posting strong efforts in big-field handicaps. Earlier in the season, he secured runner-up spots at Goodwood and York over around 1m 2f, confirming his stamina and reliability across similar trips and conditions. He's drawn in stall 6, which is considered favorable in split-pace races at Goodwood and should support his running style.

Westridge has turned a corner form-wise and comes here following a win and second place at Windsor over this trip and beyond on the last two starts. By sprinter Blue Point but proven stayer (out of a Tamayuz mare) who now has two wins from six starts on turf. Second string for in-form John & Thady Gosden yard (SR 38%). Billy Loughnane (SR 20%) rides. Conditions should suit and low in this handicap.

Ancient Rome has not run at Goodwood since winning this race in 2023 at 33-1 on his first race for Charles Hills since transferring from Andre Fabre in France. He was rated 105 then, and he has fallen recently to a mark of 100 but has been running respectably in some hot handicaps. After winning this race in 2023, he had run in Listed and Group races exclusively until this season. Jamie Spencer won on him in 2023 and will try to repeat that performance.
Take Heart won this last year and looks capable here of repeating that success again. Has been running well of late and his trainer is in form.

This horse is a perennial slow starter but hopefully a new jockey will get a tune out of him early, it's also the first time the stable have used the experienced Soumillon. This horse was sent off just 4/1 in a Group 2 at this festival last Summer when 4th of 8 and surrounded by 110+ rated horses. He gets to race off just 97 in this handicap now and yet we are getting a generous looking 18/1. Hopefully he won't give away too much ground at the start this time and he's clearly weighted to win this on a going day.
Has the highest mark in this field but has not been at his very best in the last 2 starts. However, he gained valuable experience here LTO, and the drop down in class should make life a bit easier.

Very smart type in the past, including running in a Group 1 in Meydan. He is not close to that level these days, but he has some solid form on all ground. This is his trip, and the early money for him makes him more interesting.

Now 9 years old, but SIR BUSKER took a good step forward last time out, loves a big field, enjoys it round here and is below last winning mark. Just strikes me as an outsider that ticks a lot of boxes and could outrun this price. A hold up sort so will need a gap towards the finish and some luck in running, but still worth a look at this price with the extra places.

In the last 10 runnings of this contest, 10/10 were either a 4yo or a 5yo; 0/10 had won their last race; 7/10 had run within the last 19 days, and 5/10 had recently run in the John Smith's Cup at York. This whittles the field down to English Oak and Naqeeb. Naqeeb is a 5yo gelding trained by Julie Camacho, who posted a near career-high RPR of 109 in his penultimate start at Royal Ascot, finishing 3/18 beaten 2.5l. 'Travelled strongly, in touch with leaders, smooth headway over 2f out, led narrowly under 2f out, headed inside final furlong, kept on but no extra and lost second towards finish.' That was over 1m 4f. Things didn't pan out in the John Smith's Cup (handicap) at York on his last start, but today's step down in trip to 1m 2f could see this gelding in a better light given his big effort at Royal Ascot over further. Stamina is guaranteed, and with Camacho's yard in good form of late, Naqeeb, an ex-William Haggas inmate, could outrun his odds of 28-1. Put in a combination FC with English Oak, Grey Cuban, and Castle Cove.

See, Hector has not won for a long time, but that was in G3, and has not been great since changing yards then moving to handicaps in C2, but is on a falling mark. Although he was 7/8 last time out off a 104 at 1m2f, that was showing a big improvement as was only 4L from the winner. It could be worth an EW chance off today's 101, especially as ran to third in March at Meyday in a G3 with Saffie on top. EW 5P.
Yet to win from 7 starts but has shown some promise. The jockey holds a 7lb claim, and that gives every chance in this.

Nothing special from the 3yo filly this year in her four starts, but two of three RPR ratings from her three turf runs have been far higher than what any of her rivals have been showing. This is a very weak looking selling handicap. The selection will stay this 12f trip on quick ground.
Been running over shorter distances of late. The penultimate race was over this distance, and he found himself short of room before running on.
No comment made

Win only bet here, and I couldn't let this one run without a small bet. Prescott is not notorious for first-time-out winners, usually the opposite, but its sibling won first time, and the yard is in form. Worth a squeak.

Brazilian Belle is a three year old filly who is in fine fettle with herself, and improving rapidly. She was an excellent second to Lafy Roxby here three runs back, and that filly ran a blinder to finish second at York at the weekend in a much better race than this. She then won at Thirsk, and was narrowly beaten by a Jim Goldie improver at Musselburgh last week. The pair were nicely ahead of the rest that day. Michael Dods is flying at the moment, so I have a lot of confidence in Brazilian Belle here.
Catch Cunningham evidently remains in good form, and this looks a lot more achievable than the previous two Newmarket races that resulted in 2 seconds.
Course and distance winner at a higher grade. Ran a good race at York last time out in a higher grade. Step back might suit.

The horse has run at this track and conditions at a higher mark than today's. Finished close 3rd and 4th. Recently running into form, at 10/1 looks like a nice each way play here, with a recently winning jockey in the saddle.

Has been hit/miss since winning on 2yo debut, but is nicely treated here off dropping mark of 72 and visor is going on first time today. Interesting change of jockey for this stable and very good trainer who is in form @ present, is tops here percentage wise last 5 seasons, with a impressive Lsp of 52.53, making current 12/1 solid Ew value in the race.
No comment made
Inconsistent sort, as is the norm in this lowly class. But if he is on a going day, he would have an each-way chance as he has been placed on turf from a higher mark than this.

The 5-year-old was a winner last month after coming off a 4-month break. A recent six-week break should have him freshened up for another big run. He’s a previous 10f C/D winner, and he won off a 10lb higher mark last summer. Same jockey in the saddle from that last win for this amateur riders’ handicap.
Arrives race fit and in consistent form. Owner of the horse jocked up today and seems to get the best tune out of the horse. Good chance here. Yard in modest form.

Race 4 at Beverley today is a Maiden (Class 5) for 2-year-olds over 1,006 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 2yo colt Ishimentor from the Ed Dunlop yard, and will be ridden by Joanna Mason. This son of Earthlight had a moderate debut at Nottingham last month and should improve here enough to warrant him a chance for victory today.
Wears a hood for the first time to try and help her settle in her running. Ran better last time in her second race keeping up with the pace. A small improvement/step forward could see her place.
Won well at Carlisle last time out and the 5 lbs increase might not be enough to stop him going in again here.

Ran flat over a mile and a quarter 8 days ago where the ground and trip may not have suited. Will appreciate this drop in trip being a course and distance winner off a 3 pound lower mark on penultimate start.

Race 7 at Beverley today is a Handicap (Class 5) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,496 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 10-year-old gelding Saisons D'Or from the Jedd O'Keeffe yard, and will be ridden by Jack Garritty. This son of Havana Gold is a 10-time winner and has lost none of his zest for racing, with some very decent recent form enough to warrant him some serious consideration in this field.

Wasn’t beaten far on her first start at Cork in a 5f maiden, doing well to finish as close as she did after having anything but a clear passage during the race. Not in the same form back there next time just two weeks later but bounced back to form with a close 2nd finish at Hamilton last time. She remains capable of better and can go close.

Clearly in need of debut run when no show in a class 4 novice over 5f @ Beverley. However, entitled to come on for that run/experience, that race was won by a decent sort so could have been a good race, very under used jockey replaces apprentice and very good trainer is best here with his 2yo's last 5 seasons @ 20 percent, making current 22/1 decent Ew value in the race.
No comment made

Zilfee has only seen a racecourse once, but that was a winning one at Kempton in June last year. She won by just a short head, but the form has been franked with the runner-up winning 3 times. She has to give weight to all her rivals, but Luke Catton claims 5 lbs, and she looks the most likely winner.

Only one placed effort from fifteen starts, which was at Wolverhampton over 9.5f. Has been running between 6-10f but has never run at 8f, so it could be the key to improvement, as maybe wearing a first-time hood in what is a poor quality race.
Not shown a great deal in 3 outings so far, but now handicapping from this low rating, I think we will see an improvement this evening. The stable's in form, so that is a plus factor.

Still a maiden after 4 starts between 6-7f but has improved on each run, culminating in a decent 3rd of 6 at Catterick over 6f 13 days ago, only beaten 1L. Is off a lowly mark of 46 and gets plenty of weight off rivals. Via breeding, if rains arrive, shouldn't be a problem and trainer J. Candish is 3 from 3 at the course this season.
Distance winner. Last win in Class 6 event, previously ran in Class 4 event. Now back in Class 6 event, having previously run in Class 4 event. Trainer expecting a big run here.

Looking for the four-timer, and with the jockey claim here, running from the same mark when successful here last time out in a similar race. The penultimate win has substance, so it should be hard to beat.

Just like me, currently out of form, but the last win was off a much higher mark. A drop down in trip to the last winning distance, I think, makes him a threat, which is also helped by a drop down in class.

Veteran who has been rather inconsistent this season, but his best effort so far came when 3rd off this mark over course and distance a fortnight ago. Needs to back that up but should go well in what is a very weak race if doing so.

A pretty mediocre contest as you'd expect but the outsider of the party looks a little interesting here at 22/1. Remains a maiden but has run as though conditions here might be more optimal, and has looked competitive in better races than this before fading late over 6f including at this course in May. Might have a win or two in her at this level and worth an E/W shout.

Gentle Warrior won a C3 in October and returned from a break in April to an OK fifth in C4 after a duff start. Since then, he has shown improvement with each run in C5, with the latest only missing out by a nose. Although up 3 lbs for that last run, the step back up to C4 today puts him well-weighted among today's runners.
Ran creditably on reappearance run last time, after 10 months off. Bound to come on for that run and looked a filly of promise when placed in a better race last year.
Won a decent seller 3 starts back and shaped well enough on nursery debut last time. Usual improvement should see him get his head in front here from same mark.
Made steady progress in its 3 outings so far, finishing runner-up latest. Looks capable of breaking its maiden tag this evening, and there are 3 places on offer in a 7-runner field.

Jack Rabbit Slims is a lightly raced 2-year-old gelding by Aclaim out of Velvet Jaguar. Last time at Pontefract, he was given too much to do early on and weakened to finish fifth of eleven. Ridden by David Nolan, he does show signs of progression. He should appreciate the 6f trip. The step back in grade should also suit; he was trying maidens previously, and this weaker nursery race looks winnable.
La Note Verte has won her last three races: a bumper last year and two hurdle races this season, including comfortably beating Fairbanks last time out.

Won round here on the flat last year and made an impressive reappearance 3 weeks ago when winning easily. The runner-up, a Mullins runner, franked the form when winning next time out. This is a step up in class and is the value bet against the favorite who may prefer going left-handed.
No comment made
Going for a price in this one. This grey gelding has run a couple of really good races. Not beaten far by Timeless Treaty last time out. Still room for improvement. Decent each-way price.
Collecting Coin was only beaten a neck when 2nd at the Curragh last time out and has since been gelded so could come back after a 67 day break with a win.
Made his debut in a big field 6f maiden at the Curragh when a close-up 4th. Didn’t have the clearest of passages during that race and can improve on that now. Well worth considering.
Yet to win from 6 starts but has placed 4 times, finishing 2nd on 3 occasions. That form gives an each-way chance in this.
If King of Kingsfield runs up to his last race over fences, then it would take a great improver to match this horse's ability. Reassuring to see it backed.
My Great Mate - again the yard targets this race, making a reappearance. It looks like a course specialist. It will be a good training performance here, even with conditions to suit.

Peter Fahey trained winner of a maiden point so shouldn't be altogether out of this beginners chase. Good jumping pedigree (dam was trained by Willie Mullins), related to a couple of winners. Comes here fit from a couple of recent goes in hurdles. This might suit better. Darragh O'Keeffe rides.

Thenandnow and Amelia Earhart finished 2nd and 3rd at Leopardstown over seven furlongs earlier this month. But Amelia Earhart could improve past her rival and get the win here with Jack Cleary taking off five pounds.

The model I run suggests Thenandnow can win this one. Thenandnow lines up here with the highest RPR of the 8-runner field but is not penalized for it in the weights. The eight runners all carry the same initial amount. Thenandnow is drawn in favorable stall 3, where the inside draw is statistically favorable, especially over the 7-furlong distance, which is closest to the first bend. Moel has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This was driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.
Ran Green on debut last time and is bound to improve from that run. Has decent breeding and would have a decent chance here.

Bred for speed and an early start to racing, Trusty Tycoon tackles a decent enough little maiden and attempts seven furlongs. Pivotal dam was tried over 1 mile. Small trainer does okay with sprinters. Yudish Geedharry claims 7 lbs allowance.

Listed winner at age two when with William Haggas, Alpha Capture has won once and placed twice (including at Galway) in six starts for Willie Mullins since joining the highly respected stable. Strong second at Leopardstown on reappearance this year. Slow start left him badly placed last time. Merits respect with little weight difference between all of them in this handicap.

Likes this track and was 3rd in this race last year, but returned later in the week to put things right and won that race. Is drawn well and had a satisfactory seasonal debut run two weeks ago and looks like this is the target race.

Improved on his reappearance effort when finishing a close 5th over 7f, racing from the same mark as today’s. Was given a lot to do then, but tried in a first-time tongue tie and cheekpieces combination. Can do a lot better.

Summer Snow is off a career-high mark, but two wins in her last three starts suggest she is still of interest here. She has 5 wins from 30 starts and this year has won at Leopardstown over 8 furlongs in May and at Down Royal over 7 furlongs last month. She is up 9 lbs for that win, but 7 furlongs is her ideal trip and looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

I am going to throw this one in as well as my ew tip as they both have similar traites. Has also won over c & d and just the one race this year, but it was in March and really would have liked to see a more recent run, but is drawn well with a 10lb claimer and if fit on easing ground, could run my ew and nap tip close.

Jack Cleary utilized a 5lbs claim to ride Mississippi River to win over 1 mile at Leopardstown in June. The horse (still a colt) has arguably been a bit unlucky in two starts since (beaten favorite each time). Receiving weight from older horses, different tactics may be used this time. Sole 3yo (by Lope De Vega) in the race against older horses. Aidan O'Brien trained. Strong contender.
Expecting a strong performance here from this gelding, who has been pitched in tougher races than this. Lenient handicap mark given the pattern performance too.
Has won 2 valuable handicaps in his last 2 runs and is on a steep upward curve. Still has more to offer and looks an ideal type for Galway.

A nine-year-old bay gelding trained by Dermot K. Weld, Coeur d'Or is by Dubawi out of Irresistible Jewel, showing stellar pedigree and staying power. He posted a solid fourth at Galway in this race last year, off a mark of 100 on yielding ground. His best form came in 2023 when he won the Galway Mile and the Irish Cambridgeshire at the Curragh, demonstrating his staying ability through midfield finishers. While no longer a rising star, he remains a tough and genuine competitor, often coming off the pace in a race he knows well. The going is also suited to him today.

The model I run suggests an upset from Dunum. This result has been driven by Dunum having the highest RPR of this large 14 horse race. Dunum goes out carrying a lower amount of initial weight compared to the majority of the other runners and can be advantageous over the 1m distance. Drawn in stall 2, which is statistically advantageous over the 1 mile distance, and can run the inside rail (less distance) with less weight on board. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

This bottom weight looks well handicapped to be with the first time booking of a decent Apprentice to knock another 3lb off. The horse is already a course winner off the same mark and he even followed that up with a decent 5th of 16 off a 7lb higher mark so he clearly likes it around here. The 2nd last time out also suggests he's primed to go in again soon and today could well be the day.

Bear Profit is very consistent with 5 wins and 12 other first 4 finishes in his 32 starts on the flat. He has been in excellent form recently, winning at Leopardstown in June before finishing 2nd at Curragh and 3rd back at Leopardstown 19 days ago. He was denied a clear run there, so although up another 1lb, the 7lbs claim of Nicola Burns looks significant. He looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

The handicapper has stopped dropping nine-year-old Loingseoir, but at a mark of 68, he is on his winning mark from last September at Fairyhouse. He has been competitive this season, just finishing behind rival Si Senior at Ballinrobe when 3rd last month, and previously just beaten a nose at Limerick in April when ridden by today's jockey, Nicola Burns.
Yet to win from 6 starts but has finished 3rd on 2 occasions. Needs to bounce back after disappointing on handicap debut last time. Each way chance if finding some improvement.

Lady Arwen looks interesting on first seasonal start for trainer Conor O'Dwyer. Has won two races since joining this yard off marks of 68 and 72 (OR67 today). Apprentice Jack Cleary claims five pounds. Capable at best if ready to go on first run for 237 days.

I'm more than happy with the current 20/1 odds I'm offer for Don Browne's 8 year old Mare SPECKLED MEADOW who 'Should' strip fitter for her run at Leopardstown 54 days ago after returning from a 197 day sabbatical. This Daughter of FOOTSTEPSINTHESAND finished 2nd in this contest last year off the same mark & Jockey & has ran well here on her 4 attempts. The ground currently sits at Yielding but with a bit more rain due it shouldn't bother this charge. Jockey Wayne Hassett has a 43.48% place strike rate here the past 5 years and a very impressive 60% place strike rate when riding for this yard the past year. Trainer isn't no slouch either with a decent 42.86% place strike rate the past year. 5 places, good odds with a pipe opener in the tank. I'm in.

The model I run suggests Lexington Dash can win this one. Lexington Dash lines up with the highest RPR of this larger 18-horse field but has not been penalized for it in the weights. All horses step out carrying a smaller amount of weight around this shorter 1-mile distance. Doesn't have any form on offer but has a huge price to make up for that in case it can go close. The model has issued a very low stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
